# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.

commit b7dcf0209dc8d5afaf606befe3d84093a7e4698b
Author: missingbulb <73882448+missingbulb@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Sun Aug 30 23:35:55 2026 +0300

    Auto-merge policies: expected_outcome 'none'/'pr' plus a granular, built-ins-first automerge field (#1464)
    
    * Add the auto-merge policy engine: named diff classes, pack-declared rules, fail-closed verdicts
    
    merge-policy.mjs generalizes narrow-diff's measured verdict into a policy
    vocabulary: 'nothing', 'anything', or a list of allow terms plus reject:
    terms over built-in diff classes (docs, READMEs, comment-only, tests,
    markdown line-removals, additions, GENERATED files, single-file/folder
    code) with pack-extensible rules declared as merge-rules.json data.
    Unknown names fail closed, and no granular policy can cover a change to
    the policy sources themselves. narrow-diff.mjs keeps its verdict and CLI
    on the shared primitives.
    
    Refs #1459
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017wKUYq1g3UNE65WW5KnwG4
    
    * Split the outcome ceiling: expected_outcome 'none'/'pr' plus a required may_automerge policy
    
    The contract's OUTCOMES become ['none', 'pr'], with the merge decision in
    may_automerge ('nothing' | 'anything' | a diff-class list the policy
    engine evaluates). The retired 'open-pr'/'merged-pr' normalize at the one
    door to the pair they always meant, an advisory rename at author time —
    never red CI on a member file nobody edited. verify-outcome judges the
    pair (legacy spellings included), and a dispatch surfaces the policy in
    its brief.
    
    Refs #1459
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017wKUYq1g3UNE65WW5KnwG4
    
    * Gate an armed auto-merge with a work-scope check re-measuring the diff
    
    automerge-policy-scope keys on the Claudinite-Automerge-Policy commit
    trailer a landing run stamps: no trailer, no findings — a wide PR left
    open for review stays green — and an armed branch whose diff exceeds the
    stamped policy goes red at the Stop hook and in CI before the queued
    auto-merge can fire. The verdict is the policy engine's own, with each
    refusal now structured so findings anchor at the offending file. The
    evaluator surface is published for other packs via shared-code.
    
    Refs #1459
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017wKUYq1g3UNE65WW5KnwG4
    
    * Generalize the request lane's Merge field to a policy expression
    
    An asker's Automerge: (and the item's Merge:) now carries any policy the
    engine reads — 'anything', a rule list, or the legacy 'if-narrow', which
    resolves to the narrow-diff composite. The pure work-item fence keeps the
    grammar inline (drift-guarded against normalizePolicy by test), a
    well-formed-but-unresolvable name rides through to fail closed loudly at
    the verdict, and the implement-request worker runs the generic policy CLI

# Version history

Records for `packs/claudinite-tasks/pack.mjs`'s `version` field, one row per bump.

| Version | Date | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| 60830.5 | 2026-08-30 | The auto-merge decision becomes a policy: `expected_outcome` collapses to `none`/`pr` (legacy spellings normalize at the door, advisory rename at author time) and a `pr` task declares `automerge` — `nothing`, `anything`, or a list of built-in diff classes `merge-policy.mjs` measures the actual diff against (a pack may extend them as `merge-rules.json` data; anything unresolved fails closed). Landing procedure lives only in `deliver-pr.md` — a task.md describes the changes to perform, never what happens to them. `usage-fold` stops maintaining the `merge=ours` `.gitattributes` line in-run: the pack seeds it at adoption (`seedOps`) and the advisory `generated-merge-driver` drives any repo whose own file predates that. A landing run stamps the `Claudinite-Automerge-Policy:` trailer and the new blocking `automerge-policy-scope` work check re-measures the verdict; the request lane's `Merge:` field now carries any policy expression, `if-narrow` resolving to the `narrow-diff` composite (#1459). |
| 60830.4 | 2026-08-30 | A failed run parks `failure` whatever its worker's triage marker asked for: routing the park by the marker let a worker downgrade its own non-zero exit into a non-blocking lane, so the standing slot freed and the task re-filed daily against an unfixed cause (seven copies in one member, twenty-two in another). The verdict survives as the human-facing instruction in the comment. Janitor rules E and F close a park once a later run of the same task converges clean, or once its task is no longer carried at HEAD — the verdict #1446 gave the executor, applied to the parked set it never picks (#1452). |
| 60830.1 | 2026-08-30 | A task deleted from the checkout while a run is in flight converges its item as obsolete instead of failing it to a human: the executor probes the task directory before it runs anything, and `runCodeWork` names the missing directory rather than letting Node report a missing `/bin/sh` (#1444). |
| 60827.5 | 2026-08-27 | `commentOnly` and its checkable-extension set move to `engine/checks/helpers/code-scanning.mjs`, beside the `stripComments` they were already built on; narrow-diff imports and re-exports them, so the queue's merge verdict and tidy-repo's improve-comments gate answer "comments only" the same way (#1383). |
| 60827.4 | 2026-08-27 | The terminal transition is planned as ops and executed by whichever transport the run has: REST in Actions, and the session's own GitHub tools where a subprocess has no route to them — which is every session `invoke.mjs` fires. The park for a convergence that could not run at all is fixed at the failure park, the only one that holds the task's lane (#1374). |
| 60827.2 | 2026-08-27 | A converge writes only to the item it holds: releasing a dependent a close makes due is the scheduler run's own readiness job alone, never the closing side's. `readyDependents`/`releasedBy` retire from `readiness.mjs` with no caller left (#1373, reversing #892's §15.19). |
| 60827.1 | 2026-08-27 | The request-parameter labels are gone from the code: a request's model and merge authorization are body fields, so `claude-model:*`, `claude-automerge` and the `REQUEST_LABELS` ensure-set had no reader left (#1380). |
| 60824.9 | 2026-08-24 | The scheduler run's request half no longer throws on its first real request: `parseBlockedBy` was named in `main` and never imported, unreachable while the adoption list was always empty. The blocker resolution is an exported step, so a test can drive it (#1354). |
| 60824.8 | 2026-08-24 | The request lane reads again: each mark is asked for on its own rather than both in one conjunctive `labels` filter, which had selected issues wearing both spellings and so nothing at all since #1138. Neither listing lets a failed read pass as an empty one (#1354). |
| 60824.7 | 2026-08-24 | The `engine/scheduler/` legacy-path shims are gone; the tests' legacy wire literals move to one shared module, since they are protocol a decoder must keep understanding rather than pointers (#1328). |
| 60824.6 | 2026-08-24 | The retired frequency spellings are no longer normalized — `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is emptied, so a declaration naming one fails validation instead of resolving to `daily` (#1234). |
| 60824.5 | 2026-08-24 | The drain gate counts what the run itself readied alongside what the queue read returns, so an item created milliseconds earlier can no longer be missed and left unclaimed until the next cron fire (#1340). |
| 60824.4 | 2026-08-24 | The executor stub's secrets block describes what the converge stamps there and nothing else; the reason a serialised secrets context is not used lives in `converge-workflows.mjs`, where the decision is implemented (#1331). |
| 60824.3 | 2026-08-24 | The executor workflow names its secrets again, stamped by the converge at the `# claudinite:secrets` marker: `toJSON(secrets)` is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags, and a flagged workflow parks every run behind a human approval (#1336, reversing #1301). |
===

316fc3c Close a park once a later run answers it; adopt-requested-packs lands its PR (#1454)
d9fcd5f A retry re-arms Not-before from now, and the parameters lead the issue body (#1457)

=== task.md ===
# Generic-coverage routine

Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
no PR.

## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed

This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)

So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
means "must produce a PR".

## 2. Measure the baseline

```sh
npm install && npm run test:live
```

The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
(and the gate's own headers).

## 3. Improve — the feedback loop

Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:

- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
  as produced.

If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic generic-coverage improvement found.`
and stop.

## 4. Postcondition

Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:

```sh
bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
```

- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine.

## 5. Deliver the PR

Branch `claude/generic-coverage/<date>`, commit the change plus the regenerated
GENERATED artifacts, and push. Open the PR, then hand it to the one delivery
procedure (`deliver-pr.md` in the mounted engine) and do what it says; the merge

=== task.md ===
# Generic-coverage routine

Weekly Claude routine (on a strong model), offline on a fresh clone. Goal: make the **generic**
generic extractor — `extension/event-extractors/generic-extractor.js` and the
shared `extension/event-extractors/helpers/*.js` — recover **more** of what the
dedicated per-site sources get, measured by the generic-coverage gate. **Most runs
correctly change nothing** — the gate already banks every prior win, so a new
generic win is rare and a forced or fake one is worse than none. No win → no branch,
no PR.

## 1. Scope — the strong model runs only because the cheap gate already passed

This task is a two-tier run, cheap gate first: the **scheduler** (a pure-code Action,
no model at all) ran this task's precondition (`task.mjs`, over the `commits` signal),
and only *because* it found a meaningful change did it dispatch you — a strong-model
subagent — via the `ready-for-agent` issue. Most weeks the gate skips and no strong
model ever boots; you are paid for solely on the weeks there's real work. (This is
the "cheap dispatcher front door" cost model — the scheduler precondition is that
front door, cheaper than a dispatcher session because it runs no model.)

So **you don't re-run that gate.** The dispatch issue's **Context** names the
substantive commits in the window; treat it as binding scope and don't re-litigate
whether to run. Still: **most runs correctly change nothing** (below), so "ran" never
means "must produce a PR".

## 2. Measure the baseline

```sh
npm install && npm run test:live
```

The gate prints a "bare generic value differences (informational)" block and a
per-exemplar matrix (✓ match · ~ different value · ✗ missing · — n/a): a `~` is a
concrete generic gap the extractor gets wrong, a `✗` a field it finds nothing for —
your candidate targets. This run is your pre-change reference (the committed
`generic-coverage.baseline.GENERATED.json`); don't `git stash`/rerun to re-derive
it — that conflicts on the `ours`-driver GENERATED artifacts. A committed baseline
listing **fewer** `cases` than the live run is pre-existing drift, not something
your change introduced. Gate mechanics: [the gcec pack’s RULES.md](../../RULES.md)
(and the gate's own headers).

## 3. Improve — the feedback loop

Pick one or a few `~`/`✗` gaps and close them, iterating: **hypothesize → edit only
the generic extractor / helpers → `npm run test:live` → compare to the baseline**,
until you have one or more clean wins (or conclude there are none). Every change
must clear the bars **postconditions.sh** enforces in step 4 — hold to them as you
work, because a run that trips one there is marked **failed**:

- **Generic only** (postcondition: *scope*). Key off a widely-used convention that
  would help unseen sites — display conventions (date↔time separators, start–end
  ranges, "Event @ Venue" titles, ordinals) or machine-readable signals (schema.org
  JSON-LD, OG/meta, microdata, `<time datetime>`). Lifting one `custom/<site>.js`'s
  logic or special-casing a host is out of scope: if the only beneficiary is a
  single case and the rule wouldn't fire elsewhere, it isn't generic. **The only
  files you may leave changed are `generic-extractor.js`, `helpers/*.js`, your
  covering test in `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, and the
  regenerated generic-coverage GENERATED artifacts** — anything else fails scope.
- **A real, non-regressing win** (postcondition: *win*, via the suite's gate). Every
  gated % must end **≥** its baseline and at least one strictly higher; a change
  that lifts one field but drops another isn't clean — drop it.
- **No illusory win** (postcondition: *jsdom*). The offline body-text scan reads
  `document.body.textContent`, which includes `<script>` JSON (Next.js
  `__NEXT_DATA__`), `<noscript>`, `<style>`, `<select>/<option>`, and CSS-hidden
  text — none of which Chrome's `innerText` exposes. A win matching only such
  content is illusory; a real one comes from visible text or a Chrome-read attribute
  (meta / JSON-LD / microdata / `<time datetime>`). **In step 4 you must pass every
  value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan** so this is checked.
  (Widening a scan-window cap can make a *different* case match a `<script>` blob it
  never reached — re-run the whole corpus before raising any cap.)
- **No forbidden win.** Don't invent `ctz` or `eventLengthInMinutes` (a wrong `ctz`
  is worse than none). `ctz` may only be *derived*, never guessed: two independent
  page-declared hints must agree — the contract
  `extension/event-extractors/helpers/derive-timezone.js` implements (#674/#676) —
  so never weaken its refusal rules for a coverage win. When a change fills a field
  generically, also check the cases whose dedicated source deliberately leaves that
  field EMPTY (stubhub/seetickets set no `ctz`) still come out empty — a "win"
  there silently breaks strict parity. `start`/`end` already match when they
  resolve to the same instant, so don't chase representation-only differences;
  never override a miss a unit test deliberately asserts.
- **Covered and clean.** Add or extend a case in
  `extension-test/event-extractors/extraction.test.js`, red-before-green; the full
  `npm test` must be green (postcondition: *suite*). Never weaken a test, lower the
  gate, or hand-edit a GENERATED file — commit the regenerated baseline + scorecard
  as produced.

If no clean generic win emerges, print `No generic generic-coverage improvement found.`
and stop.

## 4. Postcondition

Pass every value the change newly recovered via the body-text scan as arguments:

```sh
bash .claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/generic-extractor-improvements/postconditions.sh "<recovered value>" ...
```

- Exit 0 → the win is valid; go to step 5.
- **Non-zero → the run has FAILED.** Do not retry and do not open a PR; surface the
  failure so guiding prose can be re-introduced to this routine.

## 5. Deliver the PR

Branch `claude/generic-coverage/<date>`, commit the change plus the regenerated
GENERATED artifacts, and push. Open the PR, then hand it to the one delivery
procedure (`deliver-pr.md` in the mounted engine) and do what it says; the merge
mechanics are the gcec pack's
[merge-and-ci skill](../../skills/merge-and-ci/SKILL.md). PR body: the
hypothesis, why it's generic (which unseen sites it helps), how the jsdom trap was
ruled out, the before→after numbers, and the covering test.

Then log the run on the standing *Auto-Improvements Tracker - Generic Extractor
Coverage* issue, and `Refs` that issue in the PR.

# A thin wrapper: every decision lives in the engine modules named in the `run:`
# lines below, which converge nightly — this file does not, so it must not grow
# logic. It carries no cron; the scheduler workflow's drain is the guaranteed
# delivery and a label event is latency sugar.
name: Claudinite executor

on:
  issues:
    types: [labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      continuation_depth:
        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write
  actions: write

jobs:
  execute:
    # A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing here
    # decodes — so both ready spellings must appear for as long as any fielded
    # engine writes the legacy one (#1119).
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'

  baseline while the gate is red — a regression bundled with a case-set change can

Declare the pair on both, and express the routine's scope as a pack merge rule so the merge gate refuses what the postcondition refuses.

input.title: gcec tasks: declare the outcome/automerge pair, scoped by a pack merge rule
input.head: claude/automerge-policy-migration
input.body:
Closes #1101

Both tasks now declare the `expected_outcome` / `automerge` pair the canon's auto-merge release (missingbulb/Claudinite#1464, claudinite-tasks 60830.5) introduced, rather than the retired one-word ceilings.

**`create-extractor`** meant what `open-pr` normalizes to, so it just says it: `pr` + `automerge: 'nothing'`. A human always reviews a new extraction.

**`generic-extractor-improvements`** did *not* mean what `merged-pr` normalizes to. `'anything'` authorizes an unreviewed merge of any diff at all — including one the routine's own `postconditions.sh` would have rejected. The routine's real ceiling is that postcondition's four-path scope, so the pack declares it once as a merge rule and the task names it:

```js
automerge: ['generic-coverage-scope'],
```

The two gates are independent by design: the postcondition is a gate the run executes on itself in its checkout; the policy is re-measured by the engine against the pushed diff, which is what makes it worth having.

Verified against the canon engine, with the real declarations and the real `merge-rules.json`:

| diff | verdict |
|---|---|
| extractor + helper + covering test + both GENERATED artifacts | merge |
| a new `helpers/*.js` file | merge |
| lifting a `custom/<site>.js` | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| touching `extension/manifest.json` | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| deleting a helper | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| rewriting `merge-rules.json` or its own `task.mjs` | park — *defines auto-merge policy itself* |

Deletion parking is deliberate: `postconditions.sh` tolerates a deletion inside the scope, the merge policy does not, because deciding a helper should not exist is a reviewed change.

### Drift guard

The scope pattern now exists twice — a shell literal in `postconditions.sh` and a JSON regex in `merge-rules.json`. They cannot share a constant: the postcondition runs where no engine is loaded, and the policy engine judges a branch it never checked out. So the pack gains a blocking `generic-coverage-scope-agrees` check comparing the two byte-for-byte, watched by four red-first fixture tests in `pack.test.mjs`. It was seen firing against the live tree with one side widened, and silent against the tree as committed.

`check_the_world.mjs` on the branch: **37 blocking, 13 advisory** — identical blocking count to `origin/main` (37 blocking, 15 advisory), so this change adds none and retires two legacy-spelling advisories. The 37 pre-existing `claudinite-isolation` findings on `main` are unrelated to this change and worth a look separately.

### Folders touched

- **`.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/`** — new `merge-rules.json` declaring `generic-coverage-scope`; new `generic-coverage-scope-agrees.mjs` check, registered in `pack.mjs` and covered by four new fixture tests in `pack.test.mjs`; one new RULES.md bullet on widening the scope in both places.
- **`.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/`** — the two task declarations restated as the outcome/automerge pair.

Fleet update forced and converged; both migration PRs are up.

**Fleet update** — filed [Shepherd#353](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/issues/353) as a `fleet-baseline` work item by hand (the queue's `create-work-item.mjs` can't reach GitHub from a session), the executor picked it up and reported success. Every Claudinite member is now on `claudinite-tasks` **60830.5**: Shepherd, ClaudiniteCanary, ClaudiniteWebsite, CrosswordChat, EdFringeNow, GoogleCalendarEventCreator, LaughCounter, MissingBulbWebsite, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, VascularColoring, WIP, hitbut. HelloWorldFlutterApp and gRatio carry no declaration at all — uncovered, not a failed dispatch.

**Repos with local-pack tasks.** `search_code` returned 3; a direct scan of every member found **4** — it missed GoogleCalendarEventCreator entirely. Claudinite itself was already migrated in #1464. Of the rest:

| repo | task | was | now | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EdFringeNow | `refresh-shows`, `refresh-tickets` | `none` | *unchanged* | they commit straight to main and open no PR — nothing to merge. Validated clean against the new contract. |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | `site-stats` | `merged-pr` → `anything` | `pr` + `['single-file-code-changes']` | its whole output is four numbers in one data file |
| GCEC | `create-extractor` | `open-pr` → `nothing` | `pr` + `'nothing'` | faithful — a human always reviews an extraction |
| GCEC | `generic-extractor-improvements` | `merged-pr` → `anything` | `pr` + `['generic-coverage-scope']` | **not** faithful: `anything` would auto-merge a diff its own postcondition rejects |

That last one is where I didn't just carry the old ceiling over. The routine is an open-ended Opus loop held to a four-path scope by `postconditions.sh` — a gate the run runs on *itself*. `'anything'` authorized an unreviewed merge of any diff at all. The pack now declares that exact scope as a `merge-rules.json` rule the engine re-measures against the pushed branch. Verified with the canon engine: a real win merges, a new helper merges, and a `custom/<site>.js`, the manifest, a deleted helper, or a rewrite of the policy files themselves all park.

[ClaudiniteWebsite#375](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/375) — closes [#374](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/374) · `conformance` green


[GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1102) — closes [#1101](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/1101) · first `test` run green, the second still finishing

```
.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/
  new merge-rules.json declaring generic-coverage-scope; new blocking
  generic-coverage-scope-agrees check (registered in pack.mjs) that compares
  that pattern byte-for-byte against postconditions.sh's own allowed= literal,
  since a shell literal and a JSON regex cannot share a constant; one RULES.md
  bullet on widening the scope in both places

.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/
  both declarations restated as the outcome/automerge pair

dev/procedures/
  the two task rows in fileDescriptions.md re-derived from the declarations —
  both were already stale (a retired `hourly`, and a ceiling that was never
  open-pr)
```

content.text:
{"number":1102,"title":"gcec tasks: declare the outcome/automerge pair, scoped by a pack merge rule","body":"Closes #1101

Both tasks now declare the `expected_outcome` / `automerge` pair the canon's auto-merge release (missingbulb/Claudinite#1464, claudinite-tasks 60830.5) introduced, rather than the retired one-word ceilings.

**`create-extractor`** meant what `open-pr` normalizes to, so it just says it: `pr` + `automerge: 'nothing'`. A human always reviews a new extraction.

**`generic-extractor-improvements`** did *not* mean what `merged-pr` normalizes to. `'anything'` authorizes an unreviewed merge of any diff at all — including one the routine's own `postconditions.sh` would have rejected. The routine's real ceiling is that postcondition's four-path scope, so the pack declares it once as a merge rule and the task names it:

```js
automerge: ['generic-coverage-scope'],
```

The two gates are independent by design: the postcondition is a gate the run executes on itself in its checkout; the policy is re-measured by the engine against the pushed diff, which is what makes it worth having.

Verified against the canon engine, with the real declarations and the real `merge-rules.json`:

| diff | verdict |
|---|---|
| extractor + helper + covering test + both GENERATED artifacts | merge |
| a new `helpers/*.js` file | merge |
| lifting a `custom/.js` | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| touching `extension/manifest.json` | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| deleting a helper | park — *covered by no allow term* |
| rewriting `merge-rules.json` or its own `task.mjs` | park — *defines auto-merge policy itself* |

Deletion parking is deliberate: `postconditions.sh` tolerates a deletion inside the scope, the merge policy does not, because deciding a helper should not exist is a reviewed change.

### Drift guard

The scope pattern now exists twice — a shell literal in `postconditions.sh` and a JSON regex in `merge-rules.json`. They cannot share a constant: the postcondition runs where no engine is loaded, and the policy engine judges a branch it never checked out. So the pack gains a blocking `generic-coverage-scope-agrees` check comparing the two byte-for-byte, watched by four red-first fixture tests in `pack.test.mjs`. # Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. content.text:
Answering the question first, then one thing needs your call.

**The store-release task needs no migration.** It's a canon `chrome-extension` pack task (`.claudinite/shared/packs/chrome-extension/tasks/store-release/`), not a local-pack one, so it was never in scope for this sweep — and #1464 already handled it: `expected_outcome: 'none'`, no `automerge`, because it only *dispatches* the gated publish workflow and never opens a PR. GCEC's mounted copy is byte-identical to canon HEAD. Every canon task is on the new vocabulary; nothing outstanding there.

**But chasing it turned up something real.** The two non-`claudinite-isolation` blocking findings on GCEC's `main` are both `cer/release-workflows`, and the release pipeline is a full generation behind the pack:

- `chrome-extension-bump-version.yml` is **missing entirely** — `mode: bump` (the deliberate minor/major) doesn't exist in the repo.
- The orchestrator is the pre-bump shape: no `bump` job, no `ref` passthrough to create-package.
- `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` differs by ~157 lines — the trigger semantics changed from *"did a shipped file change since the last release"* to *"has the version on main been released yet"*, which pairs with the pack's newer `cer/version-bumped` rule (a PR raises the patch in the same PR, so merging it is what cuts the release).
- `.github/release.config` still calls itself six keys and lists five; the new standard declares five.

One correction to something I might have implied: the cron is **not** wrong here. The stub carries `30 0 * * *` for repos with no scheduler, and the check explicitly requires a scheduler-running repo like GCEC to *drop* it — GCEC is already correct on that point, with `store-release` firing the daily leg.

Worth knowing: GCEC's CI doesn't run `check_the_world`, so these findings only fire at the Stop hook — which is how `main` has been sitting red ([#648](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/648) is the open issue to add that CI job).

input.body:
`cer/release-workflows` reports two blocking findings against `main`, and reading the drift out in full shows the repo is running the pre-`bump` generation of the pack's release standard rather than being two files short of the current one.

They only surface at the Stop hook: this repo's CI runs `test`, not `check_the_world`, which is why `main` has been sitting red on them (#648 is the open issue for adding that job).

## What the checks say

```
[BLOCKING] cer/release-workflows  .github/workflows/chrome-extension-release.yml
  does not call the local reusable workflow ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-bump-version.yml

[BLOCKING] cer/release-workflows  .github/workflows/chrome-extension-bump-version.yml
  vendored reusable workflow chrome-extension-bump-version.yml is missing
```

## What is actually different

Comparing each `.github/workflows/` file against `.claudinite/shared/packs/chrome-extension/stubs/workflows/`:

| file | state |
|---|---|
| `chrome-extension-bump-version.yml` | **absent** — `mode: bump` (the deliberate minor/major raise) does not exist in this repo |
| `chrome-extension-release.yml` | pre-`bump` orchestrator: no `bump` job, no `ref` passthrough into create-package, `mode` choices are `publish/package/daily` only |
| `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` | ~157 changed lines — the release trigger moved from *"did a shipped file change since the last release"* to *"has the version on `main` been released yet"* |
| `chrome-extension-create-package.yml` | 4 changed lines |
| `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml` | 6 changed lines |
| `.github/release.config` | header says "all six keys" and lists five; the current standard declares five |

The daily-release change is the substantive one. The pack's standard is now *the version comes from the change*: a PR touching a shipped file raises the patch in the same PR (`cer/version-bumped`), so merging it is what cuts the release, and create-package no-ops unless the version on `main` has no release yet. This repo still diffs shipped paths against the latest release tag instead.

## Not a finding

The orchestrator carrying **no** `schedule:` trigger is correct and should stay that way. The pack stub ships `cron: "30 0 * * *"` for extension repos with no Claudinite scheduler; a scheduler-running repo like this one is required to drop it, because the canon `chrome-extension/store-release` task fires the daily leg and the scheduler stays the repo's only cron. `store-release` itself is current — `expected_outcome: 'none'`, byte-identical to canon HEAD.

## What closing this takes

Re-vendor the workflow set from `stubs/workflows/` (de-cronned), add the missing `chrome-extension-bump-version.yml`, reconcile `.github/release.config` against the five-key standard, and confirm `cer/release-workflows` goes silent. It changes what ships and when — the new `bump` mode writes a version and pushes it — so it wants its own reviewed PR and a deliberate look at the first release cut under the new semantics, rather than riding along with unrelated work.

---

To restate the answer to your question: there was nothing to migrate. `store-release` is a canon pack task, `expected_outcome: 'none'`, already current — it dispatches the gated publish workflow and never opens a PR, so it has no merge policy to state.

# Claudinite per-repo task scheduler — the repo's ONLY cron
# (per-project-scheduling DESIGN §3). A thin shim: all logic lives in the
# vendored engine, so this file changes rarely (schema and behavior changes ride
# the vendor refresh, not edits here). It runs hourly on a repo-hashed minute
# constrained to :10–:50 — spreading the fleet, dodging GitHub's :00 stampede,
# and staying clear of the hour boundary the slot math anchors on.
#
# The minute below is a placeholder; bootstrap/vendoring rewrites it to this
# repo's stable hashed minute in :10–:50, computed by
# `node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/hash-minute.mjs <owner/repo>`
# (scheduler-workflow-shape enforces the range; baselining re-derives the value to
# catch drift). `workflow_dispatch` allows a manual run; the concurrency group
# serializes runs so a slow run and its successor never overlap.
#
# A manual run may carry `overrides` — ONE free-form `KEY=value` string, because
# GitHub cannot declare arbitrary named inputs. It reaches the engine as
# `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, and the engine understands exactly one key:
# `FORCE_TASKS=<comma-separated task ids>`.
# It runs those tasks even though their slot has already passed, and
# WITHOUT consulting their preconditions — forcing is the operator's decision, so
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Evaluate schedule and dispatch due tasks
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Empty on every scheduled run — `inputs` is only populated by
          # workflow_dispatch. The engine reads only FORCE_TASKS out of it.
          CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES: ${{ inputs.overrides }}
        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/run.mjs

  # A scheduled run reaches no one when it goes red, so escalate a whole-run
  # failure to a human-visible `workflow-failure` issue (DESIGN §3.6,
  # gha/scheduled-failure-escalation). Converges to ONE open issue by a fixed
  # title (create-or-comment), and ensures the label first since a first-run
  # failure may precede the scheduler's own label-ensure.
  report-failure:
    needs: schedule
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:

input.title: Chrome Web Store release pipeline is a generation behind the chrome-extension pack
input.body:
`cer/release-workflows` reports two blocking findings against `main`, and reading the drift out in full shows the repo is running the pre-`bump` generation of the pack's release standard rather than being one file short of the current one.

They only surface at the Stop hook — this repo's CI runs `test`, not `check_the_world` — which is why `main` has been sitting red on them.

# The static-website pack's keys — every repo-specific value the vendored release
# pipeline reads. Explicit on purpose: nothing here is published, versioned,
# built or tested except what this file names.
#
# The site is served from the repo root, so the publish set is the part of the
# root that IS the site. Everything else at the root is how the site is MADE:
# scraper/, docs/, design-concepts/, product-wiki/, plan/design/, scripts/ and
# the agent tooling were all served by the whole-root upload this replaces, and
# are deliberately absent here.
publish_root=.

# Named in four groups: the pages and their icons; the two front-ends' code and
# styles; the planner's own paths; and the data the browser actually fetches.
#
# The code DIRECTORIES are named as directories, not file by file, and that is a
# considered trade: a file-by-file list is exact but silently breaks the site the
# day someone adds js/foo.js and forgets this file, while a directory keeps
# working. The cost is that js/__tests__, shared/__tests__ and plan/lib/__tests__
# ride along — a few KB of harmless test code on a public site, which is the
# cheaper of the two failures.
#
# The data entries are the opposite: named file by file, because the two biggest
# files under data/ are scraper INPUTS that no page ever fetches, and shipping
# them is 10.3 MB of nothing. Excluded on purpose, verified against the fetch
# call sites in js/app.js and plan/plan.js:
#   data/normalized/shows.json  7.4M  the uncompacted master; the planner loads
#                                     shows.min.json instead
#   data/prices.json            2.9M  the scraper's price cache, already folded
#                                     into the catalogue before it ships
publish_paths=.nojekyll index.html accessibility.html privacy.html terms.html favicon.ico favicon.svg apple-touch-icon.png css js shared package.json plan/index.html plan/plan.css plan/plan.js plan/lib data/venues.json data/days data/normalized/shows.min.json data/normalized/availability.min.json data/normalized/descriptions.min.json

# package.json is the single source of truth; the debug pill fetches it to show
# the running version, which is why it is in the publish set above too.
version_files=package.json

# Stamps js/build-info.js and injects the analytics beacon token — the two inline
# steps the hand-rolled deploy did, now a script that also runs on every pull
# request instead of only on a deploy.
build_command=bash scripts/build-site.sh

# The repo's own gate: unit tests, JS/Python syntax, the normalizer self-test.
# The same script the pre-commit hook runs.
test_command=bash scripts/verify.sh

# The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon token. Public by nature — it ships to every
# visitor in the page — so it is a repo VARIABLE, never a secret, which is also
# the only kind of value the pipeline will export into a build.
build_vars=CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN

9-//          "this is a new generation of the site" statement, and by this script
10-//          only on the decade wrap.
11://   ymmdd  the last digit of the UTC year, then MM then DD: 2026-12-31 -> 61231,
12-//          2027-01-01 -> 70101. The bare MMDD form this replaces is NOT
13://          monotonic across a year boundary — 1.1231.3 sorts ABOVE the next
14-//          day's 1.0101.1 — and every consumer of a version (a store, a
15://          changelog, a human) reads it as "later means bigger". The year digit
16-//          restores that: 1.61231.3 -> 1.70101.1.
17-//   n      the day's release counter: 1 for the day's first release, the
18-//          previous release's n + 1 for every further release the SAME day.
19-//          It resets with the day rather than growing forever, so the number
20-//          answers "how many times did we ship today", which is the only
21-//          question it is asked.
22-//
23:// THE DECADE WRAP. ymmdd carries one year digit, so 2029-12-31 (91231) is
24-// followed by 2030-01-01 (00101) — the one legitimate DECREASE. The major
25-// absorbs it: the wrap bumps major, so 1.91231.4 -> 2.00101.1 and the ordering
26-// holds forever. Any other decrease (a version dated in the future — a hand
27-// edit, a broken clock) is an error, not a wrap: bumping the major there would
28-// paper over a real problem and burn a major on it.
29-//

input.title: The site's release pipeline is a hand-rolled copy of the static-website standard, on its retired version scheme
input.body:
This repo already ships the `static-website` standard — date-anchored version, release-on-push, bump committed back to `main`, GitHub Pages deploy — but as its own copy rather than the pack's, and the copy is on the version scheme the canon superseded.

Nothing is red: `check_the_world` reports 0 blocking here. The pack's four `sw/*` checks simply aren't watching, because the pack isn't declared.

## What exists here now

| piece | here | the pack's |
|---|---|---|
| version bump | `scripts/bump-version.mjs` (hand-rolled) | `stubs/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs` |
| release + deploy | `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, 89 lines, ~12 version references, bump and Pages deploy in one file | `static-site-release.yml` orchestrator + `static-site-publish.yml` / `static-site-deploy-pages.yml` reusables + three composite actions |
| publish set | implicit — whatever the deploy uploads | `.github/site.config` (`publish_root`, `publish_paths`, `version_files`, `build_command`, `test_command`) |
| PR gate | none | `static-site-ci.yml` |

`static-website`'s fingerprint is the `Release static site` orchestrator, so it correctly does not claim this repo today — the pack is opt-in and undeclared, not drifted. That is why nothing reports it.

## The part with a date on it

The version here is `1.0830.51` — `<major>.<mmdd>.<n>`, four date digits. The canon scheme is `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>`, five, and `bump.mjs` says exactly why:

> `ymmdd` — the last digit of the UTC year, then MM then DD: 2026-12-31 -> 61231, 2027-01-01 -> 70101. **The bare MMDD form this replaces is NOT monotonic across a year boundary** — 1.1231.3 sorts ABOVE the next day's 1.0101.1 — and every consumer of a version (a store, a changelog, a human) reads it as "later means bigger".

So this repo is on the form the canon retired for that reason, and `1.1231.n` → `1.0101.n` goes backwards at the new year. `VERSION_RE` is `/^(\d+)\.(\d{5})\.(\d+)$/`, so `sw/version-scheme` would flag the current value the moment the pack were declared.

missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite carries the same hand-rolled pipeline and the same four-digit scheme (`1.0825.37`) — the two sites drifted together, which is the tell that this belongs centrally rather than in each repo. missingbulb/EdFringeNow is the pack-owned reference: `1.60816.1`, a real `.github/site.config`, the full `static-site-*` set, 0 blocking.

## The decision

Declaring `static-website` means running its two-question adoption interview (**hosting** — Pages from this repo, or elsewhere; **publish_set** — the exact files and folders served), writing `.github/site.config`, vendoring the pipeline, retiring `scripts/bump-version.mjs` and the hand-rolled `deploy-pages.yml`, and migrating the version to the five-digit form. In exchange the four `sw/*` checks start guarding it and the pipeline stops being this repo's to maintain.

Not urgent, and not a bug today. Worth deciding before the year boundary makes the version scheme one.

---

input.title: This repo fingerprints the `macos` pack but does not declare it, and its DMG release plumbing is unowned
input.body:
Surfaced while auditing release machinery across the fleet. Nothing is red here — `check_the_world` reports 0 blocking, 1 advisory — but two things line up that are worth a look.

## The fingerprint

The canon `macos` pack's marker is `Package.swift` at the repo root or one directory down. This repo has `mac/Package.swift`, so it matches — but `macos` is not in `.claudinite-settings.json`. The declared set is `basics`, `barriers`, `claude-code-web-users-support`, `claudinite-growth`, `claudinite-lifecycle`, `claudinite-tasks`, `git-github`, `tidy-repo`, plus the three local packs (`laughcounter`, `macos-audio`, `on-device-privacy`).

A fingerprint only ever *suspects* a pack — declaring is this repo's call, and a standing "no" is a legitimate answer. But the pack's stated territory is a direct hit:

> **belongs**: native macOS apps: app-bundle assembly, TCC usage strings, Hardened Runtime entitlements, Developer ID signing, notarization and **DMG distribution**

## The unowned plumbing

`.github/workflows/build-macos-dmg.yml` and `release-macos-dmg.yml` are this repo's own build-and-release pipeline, and no declared pack owns them. The corpus is explicit that release/deploy/versioning plumbing should be checked against a pack that owns it before a repo carries its own copy.

One thing that makes this *less* alarming than the equivalent finding in the extension and website repos: `macos` ships **no workflow stubs** — it is prose, `RULES.md` and `worldRules` only. So these workflows are not a divergent copy of a vendored pipeline the way missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator#1103 and missingbulb/CrosswordChat#352 are. There is no canonical DMG pipeline to fall behind. Declaring the pack would bring its rules and checks to bear on the signing/notarization/bundle surface, not replace these workflows.

`app-store-release` is the neighbouring pack and is **not** the right one — it covers Mac App Store submission, which `macos` explicitly excludes from its own scope and which this repo does not do.

## What this issue is asking

Decide whether to declare `macos` (via the `adopt-pack` skill, which runs its adoption interview and scaffolds), or record a standing "not planned" so the fleet's pack scan stops re-suggesting it. Either is a fine answer; leaving it undecided is what costs.

If the answer is yes, the second question follows: whether `macos`'s rules have anything to say about the two DMG workflows as they stand, or whether they are simply this repo's to keep.

content.text:
Tested against the PR's own code. `reject:under:` does compose — good discovery — but the result is decisive:

```
policy: under:extension/event-extractors
        under:extension-test/event-extractors
        under:dev/requirements/extractor/generic-coverage
        reject:under:extension/event-extractors/custom

  IN   merge   the generic extractor / a helper / the covering test / the baseline
  OUT  park    a custom site source          ← reject:under: plugs this one
  OUT  merge   the source registry              <-- WRONG
  OUT  merge   the assembler                    <-- WRONG
  OUT  merge   the generated load order         <-- WRONG
  OUT  merge   an unrelated helper test         <-- WRONG
  OUT  merge   the coverage gate itself         <-- WRONG
  OUT  merge   the coverage gate test           <-- WRONG
```

The concern in one line: `under:` scopes **folders**, but this routine's scope is a hand-picked *file set* with deliberate exclusions sitting inside those same folders — `postconditions.sh` allows `generic-extractor.js` and `helpers/*.js` but refuses `registry.js`, `assemble-events.js` and `custom/` in that very directory. The six remaining leaks are all single files, which `under:` has no way to name. The worst is `generic-coverage.js` — the coverage gate the win is *measured by*; auto-merging a change to your own scoring gate is the self-widening the engine guards against everywhere else.

This is the same distinction the PR's own comment draws: `under:` is for "the one folder an ad-hoc ask or a task is confined to", and canon's worked example (`wiki-growth`) uses it on `product-wiki/` — a whole tree the task owns outright. GCEC's routine isn't folder-shaped.

Note the two tasks separately: `create-extractor` is `automerge: 'nothing'` and has no scope for `under:` to express at all.

Simpler declaration and no drift surface, accepting that a run touching registry.js, assemble-events.js, the load order, an unrelated helper test, or the coverage gate itself would auto-merge despite its own postcondition rejecting the run.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.

content.text:
Tested both. Answering the GCEC question first, then one thing the syntax *does* improve.

**GCEC: `under:` can't express these two tasks, so PR [#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1102) stays as it is** — which your answer confirms. The reason, measured against #1474's own code:

`generic-extractor-improvements`' scope isn't a folder, it's a hand-picked file set with deliberate exclusions *inside* the folders it spans. The best possible inline-only policy — three `under:` terms plus `reject:under:extension/event-extractors/custom` (and yes, `reject:` does compose with `under:`) — still gets **6 of 11 cases wrong**, auto-merging `registry.js`, `assemble-events.js`, the generated load order, an unrelated helper test, and worst, `generic-coverage.js`/`.test.js` — the coverage gate the win is scored against. `generic-extractor.js` is a single file at a directory root, which `under:` has no way to name. The declared `generic-coverage-scope` rule gets all 11 right.

`create-extractor` is `automerge: 'nothing'` — no scope to express at all.

**But `under:` is exactly right for the other PR.** ClaudiniteWebsite [#375](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/375) currently says `['single-file-code-changes']`, which I now think I under-thought: it means *any one code file anywhere in the repo*. `site/data/` contains exactly one file, `promoted.js`, which is precisely what the worker writes — the "one folder a task is confined to" shape #1474 was built for, and the same shape as its own `wiki-growth` example.

| diff | `single-file-code-changes` | `under:site/data` |
|---|---|---|
| the recount itself | merge | merge |
| a stray edit to `site/index.html` instead | **merge** | park |
| a stray edit to `scripts/build.mjs` instead | **merge** | park |
| recount + homepage edit | park | park |

One caveat: neither repo's mount carries `under:` yet (#1474 is unmerged). Until it lands, `under:site/data` normalizes as **invalid**, which parks the PR for review rather than widening anything — the fallback #1474's own `wiki-growth` comment calls out. site-stats is weekly, so at worst one recount waits for a human.

input.title: site-stats: declare the outcome/automerge pair, scoped to the folder it writes
input.body:
Closes #374

`site-stats` carried the retired `expected_outcome: 'merged-pr'`. The contract normalizes that at its door to `pr` + `automerge: 'anything'` — an unreviewed merge of whatever diff the run produced. The task's whole output is four numbers substituted into `site/data/promoted.js`, and the worker writes that one path, so the ceiling now says so:

```js
expected_outcome: 'pr',
automerge: [`under:${PROMOTED_DIR}`],   // 'site/data'
```

Nothing about the weekly recount changes: the same PR opens and lands under the repo's delivery settings. What changes is that the merge is now *measured* rather than trusted.

### Why a path, not a count

This started as `['single-file-code-changes']`, which reads as "one data file" but actually means **any one code file anywhere in the repo** — a run that wrote a stray `site/index.html` instead of the recount would still have landed unreviewed. The honest ceiling is the path. `site/data/` holds exactly the file the worker writes, which is the "one folder a task is confined to" shape the inline `under:` scope (missingbulb/Claudinite#1474) exists for, and the same shape as that PR's own `wiki-growth` example.

Verified against #1474's policy engine:

| diff | `single-file-code-changes` | `under:site/data` |
|---|---|---|
| the recount itself | merge | merge |
| a stray edit to `site/index.html` instead | **merge** | park |
| a stray edit to `scripts/build.mjs` instead | **merge** | park |
| the recount plus a homepage edit | park | park |

### Before #1474 lands

This repo's mount has no `under:` scope yet, so the policy currently normalizes as **invalid** — which parks the weekly recount for review rather than widening anything. That is the fallback #1474's own `wiki-growth` comment calls out: never a wider merge, at worst one week of manual approval. `task-declaration-shape` is a text scan that only asserts an `automerge:` key is present and never parses its value, so CI is unaffected either way — `check_the_world.mjs` reports 0 blocking on the branch, and the single `file-placement` advisory is pre-existing and documented in `worker.mjs`'s own header. The 41 local-pack tests pass.

content.text:
Pushed and the PR body is rewritten to match. CI is running; I'm subscribed and will act on the result.

**GCEC — no change, and the reason is measured not asserted.** `under:` is a folder scope; `generic-extractor-improvements` is confined to a hand-picked *file set with exclusions inside the folders it spans*. The strongest inline-only policy possible — three `under:` terms plus `reject:under:extension/event-extractors/custom` — still answers **6 of 11 cases wrong**, authorising `registry.js`, `assemble-events.js`, the generated load order, an unrelated helper test, and `generic-coverage.js`/`.test.js` — the coverage gate the win is scored against. `generic-extractor.js` sits at a directory root, which `under:` cannot name at all. The declared `generic-coverage-scope` rule answers all 11 correctly, so [#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1102) stands as is. `create-extractor` is `'nothing'` — no scope to express.

**ClaudiniteWebsite — switched, and it caught a weaker policy I'd written.** `['single-file-code-changes']` reads as "one data file" but means *any one code file anywhere in the repo*; a run writing a stray `site/index.html` instead of the recount would have auto-merged. `under:site/data` is the actual ceiling.

```
.claudinite/local/packs/claudinite-website/tasks/site-stats/
  the automerge policy re-scoped from a file count to the folder path the
  worker writes, with the directory named once as PROMOTED_DIR
```

Two things worth flagging that I verified rather than assumed:

- **Until #1474 lands**, neither repo's mount knows `under:`, so the policy normalizes as *invalid* — which parks the weekly recount for review. Never a wider merge; at worst one week of manual approval. That's the fallback #1474's own `wiki-growth` comment describes.
- **`task-declaration-shape` won't catch a bad policy.** It's a text scan asserting an `automerge:` key exists; it never parses the value. So an unresolvable policy passes CI green and only fails closed at merge time. Safe here, but it means CI is not a guard against a typo'd policy term — possibly worth raising in the canon.

> ⚠️ Still open: [ClaudiniteWebsite#375](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/375) CI in progress after the re-scope; [GCEC#1102](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1102) green and unchanged. Both await review. Five issues filed and unstarted: [GCEC#1103](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/issues/1103), [CrosswordChat#352](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/issues/352), [ClaudiniteWebsite#376](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/issues/376), [MissingBulbWebsite#276](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/issues/276), [LaughCounter#343](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/343).

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files, comment-only changes, and history-keeping updates (a version bump, a changelog or `VERSIONS.md` row).
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.
